topic: Two DGX Spark firmware CVEs fixed in the August 2026 drop: what broke, what is fixed, patch tonight
thesis: NVIDIA just fixed five UEFI firmware vulnerabilities in the DGX Spark, three of them rated 8.2 HIGH including an out-of-bounds write an already-privileged attacker can turn into code execution, and the entire fix lands tonight through one firmware update to UEFI 1.110.13.
explanation_path: Start with what the machine is: the DGX Spark boots through UEFI firmware, the layer underneath DGX OS, so a flaw there sits below the operating system the viewer manages. Then land the event: on 2026-08-25 NVIDIA published security bulletin 5867 covering five CVEs in that firmware layer, all of them fixed in the same version, 1.110.13. Before the impact can land, the viewer needs what privileged attacker means here -- the vector is AV:L, local, with PR:H, privileges required high, which bounds the scare honestly: this is not a remote hole, it is a foothold an attacker who is already inside uses to get bigger. With that understood, the impacts of the 8.2 HIGH flaws follow: code execution, escalation of privileges, denial of service, information disclosure, data tampering. Close on the action, which is the reason the video exists: the DGX Dashboard or five terminal commands -- apt update, apt dist-upgrade, fwupdmgr refresh, fwupdmgr upgrade, reboot -- carry the machine to UEFI 1.110.13, and the viewer can check the version and run it tonight.

claims.claim: NVIDIA's August 2026 DGX Spark security bulletin addresses five CVEs dated 2026-08-25, and every one of them is fixed by updating the firmware to version 1.110.13.
claims.source_title: Security Bulletin: NVIDIA DGX Spark - August 2026

claims.claim: CVE-2026-24262 is an out-of-bounds write in the DGX Spark system firmware, scored 8.2 HIGH, where a successful exploit may lead to code execution, escalation of privileges, denial of service, information disclosure, and data tampering.
claims.source_title: Security Bulletin: NVIDIA DGX Spark - August 2026

claims.claim: CVE-2026-24263 is a NULL pointer dereference in the DGX Spark system firmware, scored 8.2 HIGH, fixed in the same UEFI 1.110.13 update.
Both CVEs affect every DGX Spark firmware version from 0 to 1.110.12, and NVD published them on Aug 25, 2026.
NVIDIA's documented manual update path is five terminal commands, and the DGX Dashboard is the recommended alternative.
claims.source_title: OS and Component Update Guide -- DGX Spark User Guide

claims.claim: The current DGX Spark software stack ships UEFI 1.110.13, the fixed version, alongside DGX OS 7.5.0 and GPU driver 580.159.03.
The attacker in both CVEs must already be a privileged local user: the CVSS 3.1 vector is AV:L/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H.
NVIDIA thanks one researcher, Alex Matrosov, for reporting four of the five flaws including both CVEs in this video.
claims.source_title: Security Bulletin: NVIDIA DGX Spark - August 2026

claims.claim: The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security republished the advisory as AV26-849, confirming DGX Spark versions prior to 1.110.13 are the affected population.

analogy_candidates.vehicle: Locked display case inside an already-locked shop
analogy_candidates.mapping: the DGX Spark is a shop with a locked front door (your OS login), and the UEFI firmware is a display case inside holding the most valuable goods; the CVEs are a flaw in the case's lock that only matters once someone is already inside the shop, but once they are, it hands them the goods, the alarm code and the keys to the till
analogy_candidates.limit: the shop analogy implies goods stay inside one room, while a UEFI compromise is S:C, scope changed, meaning the escape reaches beyond the firmware component into the whole system -- the case does not just open, it dissolves into the shop

misconceptions.myth: A firmware CVE scoring 8.2 HIGH means strangers on the internet can walk into my DGX Spark tonight.
misconceptions.reality: The CVSS 3.1 vector is AV:L/AC:L/PR:H, attack vector local and privileges required high, so the attacker must already hold privileged local access; the flaw is how a foothold escalates, not how one begins (claims 2, 3, 7).

misconceptions.myth: Ubuntu keeps my DGX Spark firmware patched automatically, same as any apt package.
misconceptions.reality: The fixed UEFI version arrives through a firmware update -- NVIDIA's documented path runs fwupdmgr refresh then fwupdmgr upgrade after the apt steps, or the DGX Dashboard, and versions prior to 1.110.13 remain vulnerable until that update lands (claims 1, 5, 9).

glossary.definition: The firmware layer that boots the DGX Spark and sits underneath the operating system, which is where all five CVEs live.
A public catalog entry giving a reported security flaw a standard ID so vendors and users refer to the same bug.
A 0.0 to 10.0 severity rating for a vulnerability; 8.2 falls in the HIGH band.
A bug where a program writes past the end of its allotted memory, letting an attacker corrupt adjacent data or code.
A bug where the firmware follows a pointer that points at nothing, which can crash the system or, in some cases, be steered into executing attacker code.
The Linux command-line tool that downloads and installs firmware updates on the DGX Spark, including the UEFI 1.110.13 fix.
The recommended graphical interface on the DGX Spark for installing system, driver and firmware updates.
An attacker who already holds elevated, local access to the machine, the prerequisite for all five CVEs in this bulletin.

suggested_outline:
Hook: NVIDIA just rated two flaws in your DGX Spark's boot firmware 8.2 out of 10 -- and the fix is five commands you can run tonight.
What the machine is: UEFI is the firmware underneath DGX OS, so these bugs live below the Linux you administrate.
The event: security bulletin 5867, dated 2026-08-25, five CVEs, every version from 0 to 1.110.12 affected, all fixed in one update.
What broke, honestly: CVE-2026-24262 is an out-of-bounds write and CVE-2026-24263 a NULL pointer dereference, both 8.2 HIGH, both turning an already-privileged local attacker into code execution and full tampering.
The honest catch: the vector says privileged local attacker, so this is not a remote hole -- it is why the box under your desk still needs the patch.
The action tonight: DGX Dashboard, or apt update, apt dist-upgrade, fwupdmgr refresh, fwupdmgr upgrade, reboot -- land on UEFI 1.110.13.
notes: Conflict: the confirmed angle describes both CVEs as out-of-bounds writes, but NVIDIA's bulletin classifies CVE-2026-24263 as a NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476); out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) applies to CVE-2026-24262 and CVE-2026-47626. The brief follows the primary source; the script should say an out-of-bounds write and a NULL pointer dereference, or two system-firmware flaws. The angle is otherwise intact: both are system-firmware flaws, both 8.2 HIGH, both fixed in 1.110.13. Tooling: web_search plus web_extract only; FireCrawl not available in this environment. 4 searches, 9 page fetches, 0 failures. ServeTheHome fetched as the independent walk-through of the same firmware-update procedure. NVD is NVD enrichment pending but mirrors NVIDIA's CNA data verbatim, including the 8.2 score.
viewer_situation: You have a DGX Spark on your desk running AI workloads, and you have never touched its firmware.
process_steps: Open the DGX Dashboard and install available updates, or open a terminal on the Spark.
Run sudo apt update, then sudo apt dist-upgrade.
Run sudo fwupdmgr refresh, then sudo fwupdmgr upgrade, and approve the UEFI 1.110.13 update when prompted.
Reboot the machine to apply the firmware update.
Confirm the UEFI version now reads 1.110.13.
objection: The CVSS vector requires a privileged local attacker, so if nobody hostile already has root on my Spark there is nothing to exploit and the patch can wait for the next maintenance window.
